title: Which Attractions in Uganda Deserve Your Time? A Region-by-Region Pick From Bwindi to Kidepo
meta_title: Attractions in Uganda: Parks, Waterfalls, Lakes and Towns
meta_description: The best attractions in Uganda by region: gorillas, chimps, Murchison Falls, Jinja, Sipi and Kidepo, with drive times, permit costs and sample routes.
excerpt: The best attractions in Uganda grouped by region, from Bwindi's gorillas and Murchison Falls to Jinja, Sipi Falls and Kidepo, with drive times, permit costs and routes for 7 to 14 days.
content:
The best attractions in Uganda are the mountain gorillas of Bwindi, the chimpanzees of Kibale, Murchison Falls on the Nile and the Kazinga Channel in Queen Elizabeth National Park. Beyond the parks, Jinja, Lake Bunyonyi, Sipi Falls and Ziwa's white rhinos add rafting, lakes, waterfalls and rhino walks.

The hard part is not finding attractions in Uganda but choosing between them, because the roads are slow and the highlights sit in different corners of the country. This guide groups the attractions in Uganda by region, gives honest drive times and current permit costs, and shows which combinations work in seven, ten or fourteen days. When you are ready to turn a shortlist into a route, our tailor-made Uganda safari packages are built around exactly these places.

Quick Facts

  • Top attraction: Mountain gorilla trekking in Bwindi Impenetrable National Park (permit USD 800 per person for foreign non-residents, checked November 2026)
  • Main airport: Entebbe International Airport, about 40 km south of Kampala
  • Best months: Roughly June to September and December to February for drier trails
  • Minimum trip: 7 days for the south-west loop; 10-14 days to add the north or Kidepo
  • Visa: Single-entry eVisa USD 50, or the USD 100 East Africa Tourist Visa for Uganda, Kenya and Rwanda (checked November 2026)

What Are the Top Attractions in Uganda?

The top attractions in Uganda fall into four groups: primate forests, savannah parks, the Nile, and the mountains and lakes. Most first-time visitors to the attractions in Uganda combine a gorilla trek, a chimpanzee trek and at least one savannah park with a boat trip, then add a lake or the Nile if time allows.

The table below lists the attractions in Uganda we are asked about most, with what each is best for and how long to allow. Drive times are from Kampala or Entebbe in normal traffic.

For a deeper look at each protected area, park by park, read our guide to the best national parks to visit in Uganda. This post looks wider, at how all the attractions in Uganda fit together on one itinerary.

Gorillas, Crater Lakes and Tree-Climbing Lions in the South-West

The south-west holds the densest cluster of attractions in Uganda, which is why almost every first itinerary heads there. Bwindi, Queen Elizabeth, Lake Bunyonyi and Lake Mburo sit along one road corridor, so you can link them without doubling back.

Bwindi Impenetrable National Park

Bwindi protects roughly half of the world's mountain gorillas and is listed by UNESCO for its ancient montane forest (see the UNESCO World Heritage listing for Bwindi). Treks start at 8am from one of four sectors, Buhoma, Ruhija, Rushaga and Nkuringo, and last from two to seven hours depending on where the family is feeding. Once you find them, you get one hour with the group.

Permits cost USD 800 per person for foreign non-residents (checked November 2026) and are sold by the Uganda Wildlife Authority, which caps the number issued per family each day. Pick your lodge only after the permit is confirmed, because the sector decides where you sleep. Our Bwindi gorilla trekking guide explains the sectors and fitness side in detail.

Queen Elizabeth National Park and the Kazinga Channel

Queen Elizabeth National Park is Uganda's classic savannah stop. The two-hour launch cruise on the Kazinga Channel, which links Lake George and Lake Edward, passes some of the densest hippo and buffalo gatherings in East Africa, with crocodiles, elephants and waterbirds on the banks. In the southern Ishasha sector, lions often rest in fig trees during the heat of the day.

Ishasha sits on the way to Bwindi's Buhoma sector, so it makes a natural game drive on the transfer day.

Lake Bunyonyi and Lake Mburo

Lake Bunyonyi is a long, terraced lake near Kabale, scattered with about 29 islands, and it is where many travellers rest after gorilla trekking. Among the quieter attractions in Uganda, it is about canoe trips between islands and ridge walks, roughly two hours from Bwindi's southern sectors.

Lake Mburo National Park, on the main road west from Kampala, is the only park in Uganda with impala and the best place to see zebra and eland on the way to the south-west. It neatly breaks the long drive west. Our 6 day Uganda safari with Lake Mburo, Lake Bunyonyi and Bwindi links all three.

Where Do You See Chimpanzees and the Mountains of the Moon?

Uganda's west, around Fort Portal, is the place for chimpanzees and high mountains. Kibale National Park has the country's most reliable chimpanzee tracking, while the Rwenzori Mountains rise on the Congo border to above 5,000 metres, with glaciers on the highest peaks.

Kibale National Park

Kibale's habituated chimpanzee communities are tracked in morning and afternoon groups, and the forest also holds red colobus, L'Hoest's monkeys and grey-cheeked mangabeys. The chimpanzee permit was USD 250 for foreign non-residents under the Uganda Wildlife Authority tariff for July 2024 to June 2026, and several Ugandan operators report a rise to USD 300; confirm the current rate before you book. Our chimpanzee trekking in Kibale guide covers timing and what the walk is like.

Rwenzori Mountains and Semuliki

The Rwenzori Mountains are a serious trekking range rather than a casual add-on: the climb to Margherita Peak takes about a week and a half with acclimatisation, while one to three day hikes reach the lower forest and bamboo zones. Our 10 day Rwenzori climb to Margherita Peak shows how the full ascent is paced.

Murchison Falls and Ziwa: The Northern Run From Kampala

Murchison Falls National Park is Uganda's largest park and the best of the attractions in Uganda for a short trip from Kampala. The Nile squeezes through a gorge only a few metres wide before plunging over the falls, and the park's northern savannah holds giraffes, elephants, lions and large herds of buffalo and kob.

The two must-dos are the boat trip to the foot of the falls and the walk to the top. Game drives are on the northern bank, reached by ferry.

Ziwa Rhino Sanctuary lies in Nakasongola District about 164 km north of Kampala, so most travellers stop there on the way to Murchison. Southern white rhinos were reintroduced in 2005, and you track them on foot with a ranger, which is rare in East Africa. Our 3 day budget Murchison Falls safari includes the Ziwa rhino walk, the boat trip and the hike to the top of the falls.

Is Kidepo Valley Worth the Journey?

Kidepo Valley National Park is worth the journey if you want a wild, almost empty savannah park and have at least four spare days. Of all the attractions in Uganda it is the most remote, tucked into the far north-east near the South Sudan and Kenya borders, with open plains ringed by mountains.

Kidepo's wildlife includes lions, buffalo herds, elephants and several species that are hard to find elsewhere in Uganda, such as ostriches and, with luck, cheetahs.

The honest trade-off is distance: by road it takes most of two days each way from Kampala, which is why many travellers fly in. Our 4 day Kidepo Valley safari from Entebbe goes by road with a night on the way, starting from USD 1,789 per adult, for travellers happy to see the country change outside the window.

Attractions in Uganda Beyond the National Parks

Some of the best attractions in Uganda are not in national parks at all: the source of the Nile at Jinja, the waterfalls at Sipi on Mount Elgon and the swamps around Entebbe. They suit adventure, culture and rest days between long drives.

Jinja and the Source of the Nile

Jinja, about 80 km east of Kampala, sits where the Nile leaves Lake Victoria. Boat trips run to the spot marked as the source, and the river below offers white-water rafting, kayaking, tubing and stand-up paddleboarding. Groups planning a rafting day can read our guide to Jinja rafting for groups. For many visitors it is one of the most fun attractions in Uganda.

Sipi Falls and Mount Elgon

Sipi Falls is a series of three waterfalls on the north-western slopes of Mount Elgon, about 270 km north-east of Kampala; the main fall drops roughly 95 metres. A guided half-day walk visits all three through coffee farms, and Mount Elgon National Park above has multi-day treks.

Kampala, Entebbe and Lake Victoria

Kampala and Entebbe are usually just arrival and departure points, but a day here is well spent. Mabamba Swamp, west of Entebbe, is one of the most reliable places in East Africa to see the shoebill from a canoe, and the grey crowned crane, Uganda's national bird, is common in the surrounding farmland. In Kampala, the Namugongo shrine and the craft markets are cultural attractions in Uganda that fit into a spare afternoon.

How Many Days Do You Need to See Uganda's Highlights?

Seven days is the realistic minimum to see the core attractions in Uganda: chimpanzees, a savannah park with a boat cruise, and gorillas. Ten days adds Murchison Falls or Lake Bunyonyi, and two weeks lets you combine the north and south-west without exhausting road days.

Trip lengthRouteWhat you see
7 daysEntebbe – Kibale – Queen Elizabeth – Bwindi – EntebbeChimps, Kazinga Channel, Ishasha lions, gorillas
10 daysAdd Lake Mburo and Lake Bunyonyi, or start with Ziwa and MurchisonAdds zebra and impala or rhinos and the falls
14 daysZiwa – Murchison – Kibale – Queen Elizabeth – Bwindi – Bunyonyi – MburoMost major parks, one or two gorilla treks
4 extra daysKidepo Valley by road or flightRemote savannah and Karamojong culture

Visas, fees and health checks

Most visitors need a Uganda visa, applied for online: the Uganda Immigration tourist visa page gives the single-entry tourist visa fee as USD 50, while the UK government's Uganda entry advice notes the USD 100 East Africa Tourist Visa, valid for 90 days across Kenya, Rwanda and Uganda (both checked November 2026).

Park entry for foreign non-residents was USD 40 to 45 per adult per day at the main parks under the Uganda Wildlife Authority tariff for July 2024 to June 2026; confirm current rates before booking, as new activity prices have been announced. On 2 October 2026 Uganda Immigration posted a notice that a yellow fever certificate is no longer mandatory for entry, but airlines and onward countries may still ask, so check with your travel clinic.

Insider Tips

  • Permit first: Secure the gorilla permit before booking lodges; the sector it is issued for decides your route
  • Fly one leg: A domestic flight between Bwindi and Entebbe saves a full day of driving at the end of a trip
  • Pair by region: Murchison and Ziwa pair well; so do Kibale, Queen Elizabeth and Bwindi; trying to do both in a week means too many road hours
  • Rest after trekking: A night at Lake Bunyonyi or Lake Mburo after Bwindi makes the drive back far easier

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the most popular attractions in Uganda?

The most popular attractions in Uganda are mountain gorilla trekking in Bwindi Impenetrable National Park, chimpanzee tracking in Kibale, the boat trip to the foot of Murchison Falls and the Kazinga Channel cruise in Queen Elizabeth National Park. Outside the parks, Jinja and the source of the Nile, Lake Bunyonyi and Sipi Falls draw the most visitors.

How many days do I need to see Uganda's main attractions?

Seven days covers the classic south-western loop of Kibale, Queen Elizabeth and Bwindi, with one chimpanzee trek, one boat cruise and one gorilla trek. Ten to twelve days lets you add Murchison Falls and Ziwa in the north or Lake Bunyonyi in the south. Kidepo needs at least four extra days by road.

Are there attractions in Uganda besides gorillas?

Yes. Many attractions in Uganda have nothing to do with gorillas: the Nile at Jinja for rafting and kayaking, the three Sipi Falls on Mount Elgon, rhino tracking on foot at Ziwa, the Rwenzori Mountains, Lake Bunyonyi's islands and the shoebill swamps near Entebbe. Kidepo Valley is one of East Africa's emptiest savannah parks.

How much does a gorilla permit cost in Uganda?

A Uganda gorilla trekking permit costs USD 800 per person for foreign non-residents (checked November 2026), and a gorilla habituation experience costs more. Permits are sold by the Uganda Wildlife Authority and are limited each day, so book several months ahead for June to September and December to February, and confirm the current tariff before paying.

When is the best time to visit Uganda's attractions?

The best time to visit most of Uganda's attractions is during the drier months, roughly June to September and December to February, when forest trails are less muddy and savannah game viewing is easier. Uganda is a year-round destination, though, and the wetter months bring greener scenery, fewer visitors and easier permit availability.

Final Thoughts

With one week, the Kibale, Queen Elizabeth and Bwindi loop shows the attractions in Uganda that made the country famous, with few wasted road days. With more time, Murchison and Ziwa, Jinja or the long road to Kidepo turn a primate trip into a full tour of the country.
